'''Ikutachi''' (生大刀) is a sword appearing in {{ill|Japanese mythology|ar|أساطير يابانية|ast|Mitoloxía xaponesa|az|Yapon mifologiyası|bjn|Mitologi Japang|ca|Mitologia japonesa|cs|Japonská mytologie|de|Japanische Mythologie|el|Ιαπωνική μυθολογία|eo|Japana mitologio|es|Mitología japonesa|eu|Japoniar mitologia|fa|اسطوره‌شناسی ژاپنی|fi|Japanilainen mytologia|fr|Mythologie japonaise|he|מיתולוגיה יפנית|hi|जापानी पौराणिक कथाओं|hr|Japanska mitologija|hu|Japán mitológia|hy|Ճապոնական դիցաբանություն|ia|Mythologia japonese|id|Mitologi Jepang|it|Mitologia giapponese|ja|日本神話|jv|Mitologi Jepang|ka|იაპონური მითოლოგია|ko|일본 신화|la|Mythologia Iaponiae|lt|Japonų mitologija|min|Mitologi Japang|mk|Јапонска митологија|ms|Mitologi Jepun|my|ဂျပန်ဒဏ္ဍာရီ|nl|Japanse mythologie|no|Japansk mytologi|or|ଜାପାନୀ ଧର୍ମକଥା|pl|Mitologia japońska|pt|Mitologia japonesa|ro|Mitologia japoneză|ru|Японская мифология|sh|Japanska mitologija|simple|Japanese mythology|sk|Japonská mytológia|sr|Japanska mitologija|sv|Japansk mytologi|szy|nu Lipun a micidekay a kungku|tl|Mitolohiyang Hapones|tr|Japon mitolojisi|uk|Японська міфологія|uz|Yapon mifologiyasi|vi|Thần thoại Nhật Bản|zh|日本神話|qid=Q814158|lt=Japanese mythology}}. It is a {{ill|大刀|ja|大刀|pl|Daikatana|zh|大刀|qid=Q1224104|lt=tachi}} that {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}} brought back from {{ill|Ne no Kuni|ja|根之堅州国|qid=DELETED_QID}} and is mentioned only in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}.

In modern contexts, it is often written as 生太刀, but since tachi refers to curved swords from the Heian period onward, the term 大刀 is used for the straight swords of mythology and ancient artifacts, such as chokutō.

== Mythology ==
When {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}} fled to {{ill|Ne no Kuni|ja|根之堅州国|qid=DELETED_QID}} to escape the pursuit of his brothers, the {{ill|Yaso-gami|ja|八十神|qid=Q65249011|lt=Yasogami (80 gods)}}, he encountered {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須勢理毘売命|lt=Suseribime}}, the daughter of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}. The two deities fell in love at first sight.

However, Susanoo imposed various trials upon Ōkuninushi, some of which nearly cost him his life. In one instance, Ōkuninushi pretended to remove centipedes from Susanoo's hair, waiting until Susanoo fell asleep. Then, he tied Susanoo’s hair to the pillars and attempted to flee with the sacred treasures, including the '''Ikutachi''', '''Ikuyumiya''' (生弓矢), '''Amanokaguyumi''' (天詔琴), and Suseribime herself. <ref>{{Cite book |language=ja |author=Tamio Tobe|title=日本神話 - 神々の壮麗なるドラマ |publisher=Shinkigensha |series=Truth In Fantasy 63 |date=October 2003 |isbn=978-4-7753-0203-3 |page=88 }}</ref>

As they fled, the Amanokaguyumi struck a tree and produced a loud sound, waking Susanoo, who pursued them to the {{ill|Yomotsu Hirasaka|fr|Yomotsu hirasaka|it|Yomotsu Hirasaka|ja|黄泉比良坂|ko|황천비량판|th|โยโมสึ ฮิระซากะ|qid=Q22084535|lt=Yomotsu Hirasaka}}, the boundary between Ne no Kuni and Ashihara no Nakatsukuni. There, Susanoo halted and proclaimed, "Use the tachi and bow to subdue the Yaso-gami who disobey you. Drive them into the mountains and rivers. You will become Ōkuninushi, the Utsushikunidama deity, and build a grand palace to live with Suseribime as your wife."

After receiving his new name, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}} used the Ikutachi and Ikuyumiya to defeat the Yaso-gami and became the ruler of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni.
